title: bleary-eyes-quick-ops-manual
content:
Shift: 01:00-09:00 PST (w/ Jordan -> Riley handoff)
Location: home laptop, coffee = present
Purpose: quick personal ops cheat / temporary procedures while we triage KV-cache memory growth (see SRE-1421). Not a polished doc — scribbles to pass to whoever picks this up.

OVERVIEW / CURRENT STATE
- Symptom: inference-runtime pods (prod cluster, us-west1) exhibiting steady mem growth over ~36h. Not OOMing yet but tail latency spikes and occasional 502s from redwood-api.
- Impact: small portion of hosted API traffic (~2-4%) hitting affected nodes; autoscaler keeps adding pods but they still pick up cached state and memory climbs.
- Suspected cause: prefix/KV cache TTL handling combined with recent memcache client bump (libkv v2.1.0).
- PagerDuty: PD-34 oncall rotation. Slack: #sre-oncall (pings go there and to @oncall-alert).

QUICK CHECKS (first 10m)
- Check overall cluster health: kubectl get nodes;kubectl top nodes | sort -nr -k3
- Pod list: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | egrep "inference-runtime|redwood-api"
- Metrics endpoints: curl https://prometheus-usw1.redwood.internal/api/v1/query?query=container_memory_rss_bytes%7Bpod%3D%22inference-runtime%22%7D (or view in Grafana board: SRE -> inference runtime)
- Check KV cache metric on a suspect pod: kubectl -n inference exec -it <pod> -- curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache_size
- Active requests / latency: Grafana -> hosted-api / per-route latency (look for 95/99 spikes)

TEMP WORKAROUNDS (fast, reversible)
1) Route small fraction of traffic away from affected nodes (canary fallback):
   - Use redwoodctl (ops CLI): redwoodctl route update --service hosted-api --policy fallback=model-small:v2 --percent 10 --duration 30m
   - Verify traffic distribution in Console -> routes.
2) Restart inference-runtime pods one-by-one to shed leaked memory (non-disruptive if rolling):
   - kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime
   - Monitor pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -w | grep inference-runtime
   - Expected: pods recycle and memory resets; if memory rises again quickly, revert and escalate to prod infra.
3) Disable aggressive local caching (temporary config flip):
   - Edit configmap (inference-runtime-config) TTL from 48h -> 30m for prefix cache. kubectl -n inference edit configmap inference-runtime-config (search: prefix_cache_ttl)
   - Restart only if config requires it.

ESCALATION PATH
- If rolling restarts do not bring memory under control within 30m: escalate to on-call infra eng (Riley Park). Call if < 15m to degrade.
- Contact list: Riley Park (pager/phone), Maya Patel (platform), SRE lead: Tomas Rivera.
- Open a P0 ticket: SRE-1421 (append notes, time, commands run, logs).

RECOVERY PLAY (if situation worsens)
- Full fallback to model-small for burst traffic: redwoodctl route update --service hosted-api --policy fallback=model-small:v2 --percent 100 --duration 60m
- Scale up reserved capacity (dedicated pool) temporarily: ops-ui -> Dedicated -> increase pool us-west1-d by +2gpus (requires approval for charge)
- If persistent OOMs: k8s node drain plan (coordinate with infra).

DEBUG COMMANDS / LOGS
- Tail logs for a pod: kubectl -n inference logs -f deployment/inference-runtime --tail=200 | grep -i cache
- Get goroutine / heap dump (runtime endpoint): kubectl -n inference exec -it <pod> -- curl -s localhost:9090/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap-$(date +%s).dump (scp/collect)
- Check latest image: kubectl -n inference describe deployment inference-runtime | grep Image
- Check memcache client version in image: docker run --rm image:tag sh -c "cat /app/requirements.txt | grep libkv"

KNOWN WORKAROUNDS (notes to self)
- There is a hotfix branch in infra repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/512 — it pins libkv to 2.0.3 and changes TTL behavior. Not yet promoted to prod.
- Local dev repro: run small-load.sh with redis-mock, observe eviction not happening when prefix length > 3. Added to SRE-1421.

SHORT-TERM TODOs (for next on-call)
- [ ] Monitor mem growth for 3 rolling restarts; if reappears, leave pods restarted and escalate.
- [ ] Patch staging with PR #512, run soak for 24h.
- [ ] Add a Prometheus alert: kv_cache_growth_rate > 10%/10m for 3 nodes -> page.
- [ ] Draft a clear rollback plan for PR 512 (who approves, quick steps).

MESSAGING / COMMUNICATION
- Slack draft to post if visible customer impact: "Heads up — we are investigating memory growth in inference-runtime that may cause intermittent 502s for a small subset of hosted API traffic. Mitigation in progress (rolling restarts + temporary route fallback). Will update in 15m. PD-34."
- Customer comms owner: @SupportOps (Maya), coordinate with CS if we need a public status page note.

PERSONAL NOTES TO NEXT: 
- If you see steady +5–10% mem growth within 1 hour after a restart, do NOT restart repeatedly — that creates a thundering restart. Instead: flip to model-small fallback, scale dedicated pool, and escalate.
- I left a snippet in my home laptop at ~/ops-scripts/quick-roll.sh that does the rollout and checks logs; password in 1Password (sre/quick-roll).

RANDOM SCRATCHES (brain dump)
- Could this be due to the new attention cache keys when sequence length > 1024? Check model variants that changed cache key format last week (see models/rollout-2026-02-05).
- Add a lightweight health endpoint that returns kv_cache_size and last_eviction_ts for quick grepping. (small infra ask)

END / Handoff checklist
- Confirmed rolling restart started at 02:15 and 4/6 pods recycled by 02:25.
- Left Grafana alert muted for 10m while tests run.
- Pushed a slack note to #sre-oncall at 02:28.

If you pick this up: ping me (Jordan) on Slack if anything odd or if you want me to run the heap dump collection. Good luck — get sleep later.
